solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Swimming attire is so out of place in church

indicators.note: letters that are out of place are not where they belong, so they must be rearranged
the rearranged letters sit inside the abbreviation for the church

blocks.note: CE is the Church of England
the two short words, taken letter by letter

explanation.surface: Someone turns up to a church service in a swimsuit, to general disapproval.
explanation.walkthrough: The jumbled IS SO goes between the C and E of CE to make COSSIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Cossie is informal British and Australian slang for a swimming costume.

clue.text: Informal party — a king's gone (got up, being very old)

indicators.note: something gone has left, so those letters are taken away from the party word

blocks.note: an informal beach party where clams are cooked
K is king in chess and cards

explanation.surface: A casual gathering is missing its king, who has gone off somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove A and K from the middle of CLAMBAKE to leave CLAMBE.
explanation.definitionFit: Clambe is an obsolete past tense of climb, so it meant climbed or rose up long ago.

clue.text: "Lousy trains!" — let out a snicker

indicators.note: lousy means poor or bad, so the word is taken in a bad, disordered form
to let something out is to release it, so that letter leaves the word

explanation.surface: A commuter grumbles about the awful trains and sniggers.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the A from TRAINS and rearrange TRINS.
explanation.definitionFit: Snirt is a Scots word for a suppressed laugh, which is just what a snicker is.

clue.text: Nasty dig seen as old-fashioned scorn

indicators.note: something nasty is in a bad state, so these letters are messed up and reordered

explanation.surface: A cruel jibe is taken as an outdated form of contempt.
explanation.definitionFit: Sdeigne is an obsolete Spenserian spelling of disdain, used as a verb meaning to look down on.

clue.text: Old artificer dressed in green

indicators.note: to dress something is to prepare or arrange it, so these letters are set out afresh

explanation.surface: A craftsman of former times wears green clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Enginer is an obsolete form of engineer, an old word for a maker or contriver of machines.

clue.text: A cooper dealt with fellows, showing skill

blocks.note: read as copper, whose chemical symbol is Cu

explanation.surface: A barrel-maker deals skilfully with his workmates.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay needs copper (Cu); the clue as recorded shows cooper, very likely a slip in transcription.
explanation.definitionFit: Acumen is keen insight or shrewdness, a kind of practical skill in judgement.

clue.text: Rulers making one horrified, no end

indicators.note: with no end, the final letter of the word is cut off

blocks.note: a person who is horrified is aghast

explanation.surface: Tyrannical rulers leave someone endlessly appalled.
explanation.walkthrough: AGHAST loses its last letter T.
explanation.definitionFit: Aghas are Turkish or Ottoman commanders and chiefs, so they are rulers or officials.

clue.text: Bent piece of equipment turning up in base but useless

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of words that follows
in a down clue turning up means reading from bottom to top, so backwards

blocks.note: the letters spanning the end of the first word and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A broken item of kit turns out to be worthless at the base.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the run E-BUT-U from base but useless backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A U-tube is a laboratory glass tube bent into the shape of the letter U.

clue.text: State penetrated by river and sea

indicators.note: something penetrated has another thing pushed into it, so a letter goes inside the state

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A state is crossed by a river and bordered by the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Marine as an adjective means of the sea, and as a noun it can mean a seascape picture.

clue.text: Indonesian working on site

indicators.note: letters that are working are in motion and so get reorganised

explanation.surface: An Indonesian labourer is busy on a building site.
explanation.definitionFit: A nesiot is an islander, and an Indonesian lives on one of the islands of the archipelago, so is an example.

clue.text: Sound by deer in road — people here may be put off

definitions.text: people here may be put off

indicators.note: the sound and deer pieces go inside the word for road

explanation.surface: A bell rings beside a stag standing in the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' simply places one piece next to the other. 'Sound' looks like a body of water to land beside, but it is a noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Passengers are set down from a boat at a landing stage, and put off is a nautical phrase for dropping them ashore.

clue.text: Over-regulator disregarding fools is one ultimately dismissed

indicators.note: to fool is to trick or muddle, so the remaining letters are jumbled
what is dismissed is sent away, so those letters leave the long word
ultimately means at the very end, so only the last letter of the word is wanted

blocks.note: taken as written, to be removed
the final letter, to be removed

explanation.surface: A bureaucrat who ignores idiots is eventually sacked himself.
explanation.walkthrough: Take I, S and E out of DISREGARDING and rearrange the rest. Thomas Gradgrind is the fact-obsessed schoolmaster in Dickens's Hard Times.
explanation.definitionFit: A gradgrind is someone who rules life by hard facts and rigid rules, named after the Dickens character.

clue.text: Lincoln? More than one tree is seen across the far side of it

indicators.note: a word seen across another lies over it, holding it inside

blocks.note: points to where IS goes: across the last letter of the Lincoln name, so it adds no letters

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about Lincoln, a place where several trees stand across the far side.
explanation.walkthrough: IS goes across the far side of it, meaning the last letter of ABE: AB followed by I(E)S.
explanation.definitionFit: Abies is the botanical genus of firs, so the name covers many trees rather than one.

clue.text: Being braver, eat nasty rodent

indicators.note: something nasty is in a bad state, so these letters are messed about

explanation.surface: Feeling bolder, someone eats a horrible rodent.
explanation.definitionFit: The beaver rat is an Australian water rat, so it is a kind of rodent.

clue.text: Students getting bishop in knots

indicators.note: to get something is to take it in, so the students' letters hold the bishop

explanation.surface: Students get themselves into a muddle over a bishop.
explanation.walkthrough: A bishop is styled the Right Reverend, abbreviated RR.
explanation.definitionFit: A nurr is a knot or knob in wood, so nurrs are knots.

clue.text: Big circle in which soldier entertains Queen and one princess

indicators.note: to entertain guests is to have them in, so the soldier holds the other pieces

blocks.note: a soldier is a man in the ranks

explanation.surface: A soldier plays host to the Queen and a princess.
explanation.definitionFit: A meridian is a great circle of longitude passing through both poles.

clue.text: People in toilet wasting time

indicators.note: to waste something is to lose it, so that letter disappears

blocks.note: the gents is a British name for a men's public toilet
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: People hang about in the public toilet killing time.
explanation.definitionFit: A gens is a Roman clan, a people sharing a name, and the same form serves as its plural.

clue.text: Disreputable house needing to arrange fencing

blocks.note: ken is old slang for a house, especially a thieves' den
to do is to arrange or see to

explanation.surface: A house of ill repute has to set up a fence around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Kendo is the Japanese martial art of fencing with bamboo swords.

clue.text: Good part of church to the west — see old Gospel

indicators.note: in an across clue going west means going left, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: the main body of a church
Ely is a cathedral city, so a bishop's see

explanation.surface: Directions inside a church: a good part lies to the west, near the old Gospel.
explanation.walkthrough: A see is a bishop's diocese, and the cathedral city of Ely is one.
explanation.definitionFit: Evangely is an obsolete word for the gospel, from the Greek for good news.

clue.text: Learner less considerate and more aggressive?

blocks.note: L for learner, as on a British L-plate
airy can mean flippant or offhand

explanation.surface: A learner driver being thoughtless and pushy.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a slang definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Lairy is British slang for loud, flashy and spoiling for a fight, so lairier means more aggressive.

clue.text: Sex symbols giving wrong signal, taking maiden in

indicators.note: something wrong is not in its proper state, so these letters are rearranged
to take something in is to hold it inside

blocks.note: M is a maiden over in cricket scoring

explanation.surface: Suggestive emblems send out the wrong message by drawing a young woman in.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange SIGNAL as LINGAS and put M inside before the final S. The final 'in' completes the container indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: A lingam is a phallic emblem of the Hindu god Shiva, a symbol of generative power.

clue.text: Resist work and attitudinise

blocks.note: OP is short for opus, a work
to strike an attitude is to pose

explanation.surface: Someone fights back by working and striking poses.
explanation.definitionFit: To oppose is to set oneself against something, the same as resisting it.

clue.text: A comet's somehow losing energy as an orbiter

indicators.note: somehow says the letters arrive in some unspecified new order
what is lost is no longer there, so that letter is dropped

blocks.note: E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A comet fades as it circles the sun.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove E from A COMET'S and rearrange what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: A comsat is a communications satellite, which orbits the Earth.

clue.text: Old traders providing duke with swords

explanation.surface: Merchants of the past supplied a duke with his swords.
explanation.definitionFit: Drapiers is an old spelling of drapers, dealers in cloth.

clue.text: Daisy's place? Has sat on the move

indicators.note: letters on the move are shifting around into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone named Daisy gets up from her seat and walks off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daisy' reads like a woman's name, but it is the flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount Shasta in California gives its name to the Shasta daisy, so it is the daisy's place.

clue.text: Dig quietly before rain

blocks.note: p is piano, softly in music
roke is a dialect word for mist or drizzle

explanation.surface: Do some digging quietly before the rain comes.
explanation.definitionFit: Proke is a dialect verb meaning to poke or prod, as in a dig with the elbow.

clue.text: Jock's to appear in outfit when meeting ambassador

blocks.note: kit is a set of clothes

explanation.surface: A Scot must dress properly to meet an ambassador.
explanation.walkthrough: Jock is a nickname for a Scot, flagging a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: Kithe is Scots for to make known or show oneself, so to appear.

clue.text: Tack to secure something round, a tiny thing

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast, so the tack holds the round letter inside

blocks.note: a tack is a small pin

explanation.surface: A drawing pin holds down a small round object.
explanation.definitionFit: A pion is a subatomic particle, a pi-meson, about as tiny as things get.

clue.text: Strong feeling of regret around hospital

indicators.note: the regret word goes around the hospital letter, holding it inside

blocks.note: H for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: Deep sorrow is felt at a hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: Pithy usually means concise, which hides its older sense of forceful.
explanation.definitionFit: Pithy, besides meaning concise, has an older sense of forceful or vigorous, hence strong.

clue.text: Marble that is easy to deal with

blocks.note: a taw is a large shooting marble

explanation.surface: A marble that is simple to handle.
explanation.definitionFit: Tawie is a Scots adjective for a tractable, docile animal, one that is manageable.

clue.text: Hello! — publication with anecdotes in a style of writing

blocks.note: a rag is a low-grade newspaper
ana are collected anecdotes or sayings

explanation.surface: Hello! magazine is written in a chatty, gossipy style.
explanation.walkthrough: Hello! is a British celebrity magazine, which makes the surface plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: Hiragana is the cursive Japanese syllabary used for native words, a form of script.

clue.text: They get hot cooked courses maybe, but no starter

indicators.note: with no starter the first letter is left off

blocks.note: roasts are cooked dishes, an example of courses

explanation.surface: Some cooked dishes come out piping hot, though not the first course.
explanation.walkthrough: ROASTS loses its first letter R. 'Starter' plays on the first course of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Oasts are kilns for drying hops, so they are heated.

clue.text: Wife in evil society — they house prostitutes

indicators.note: the wife letter goes inside the word for evil

explanation.surface: A wife moves in wicked circles that keep women of the street.
explanation.walkthrough: W goes inside BAD, then S follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Bawds were brothel keepers, people who kept women for hire.

clue.text: German veteran — this hamlet's organised to accommodate fifty

indicators.note: to organise things is to put them into a new order
to accommodate is to make room for, so another letter is taken in

blocks.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A village is reorganised to house fifty old soldiers from Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: A Stahlhelmist was a member of the Stahlhelm, a nationalist league of German ex-servicemen after the First World War.

clue.text: Reverse of thanks evident in weird restaurant

indicators.note: the reverse of a word is that word read backwards
something evident in another is seen inside it

explanation.surface: Diners at a strange restaurant show no gratitude at all.
explanation.walkthrough: Ta is British informal thanks, and eery is an accepted variant of eerie.
explanation.definitionFit: An eatery is an informal word for a restaurant or café.

clue.text: Flowering plants making dearest endlessly excited

indicators.note: endlessly means without an end, so the final letter is dropped
excited things are stirred up, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Flowers that make your sweetheart thrilled.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the T from DEAREST and rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Reseda is the genus of mignonette, so the name covers a group of flowering plants.
